dedupe_keys.name: bundesnetzagentur supply interruption statistics for german electricity and gas networks reports under section 52 enwg saidi

description: Under section 52 of the German Energy Industry Act (EnWG), every electricity and gas network operator, whatever its size or location, must report to the Bundesnetzagentur by 30 April each year the supply interruptions in its network in the previous year, with the time, duration, extent and cause of each interruption, recorded per network area. Reports are submitted through the Energiedaten portal or an XML web service, with field descriptions and general rulings of 2006 for electricity and 2008 for gas setting the format. The agency publishes the evaluated results as electricity and gas indicator pages. The German Environment Agency, reading this interruption statistics for its climate adaptation monitoring, describes it as covering interruptions longer than three minutes on the medium and low voltage levels, with causes such as atmospheric effects and force majeure, and reports that the weather-related non-availability was highest in 2021 at almost 23 minutes per final consumer, mainly from storm Bernd. Coverage is Germany. The pages are free; no licence is stated. Caveats: the indicator pages refused automated access on 26 September 2026, so their tables and file formats were not read here. Simulation uses are reliability baselines and weather-related outage trends for German grid resilience and adaptation studies. Related records: data-smard-electricity-market-data-germany is another Bundesnetzagentur data service.
